---
title: "Chart factories"
---

Attaviz factories turn summarized pandas DataFrames into publication-ready
Altair charts. Enable the theme once before creating charts:

```python
import attaviz

attaviz.enable()
```

Every factory returns an ordinary Altair chart. Use Altair directly after the
factory when a chart needs customization outside the common editorial path.

## Bar

`bar()` creates horizontal bars and requires one row per category.

```python
chart = attaviz.bar(
    data,
    category="country",
    value="population",
    title="Population by country",
    subtitle="Millions, 2025",
    sort="descending",
    labels=True,
    highlight="Indonesia",
    value_format="auto",
    width="responsive",
)
```

`sort` accepts `"ascending"`, `"descending"`, `"data"`, or an explicit
category sequence. Duplicate categories raise an error rather than being
aggregated silently.

## Line

`line()` creates one line or uses `series` to identify multiple lines.

```python
chart = attaviz.line(
    data,
    x="year",
    y="population",
    series="country",
    highlight="Indonesia",
    end_labels=True,
    points=False,
    zero=False,
)
```

Each x value must be unique for a single line. With `series`, every
`(x, series)` pair must be unique. Missing y values create visible gaps.
Up to five series use end labels; larger charts use a legend.

## Scatter

```python
chart = attaviz.scatter(
    data,
    x="income",
    y="life_expectancy",
    label="country",
    series="region",
    highlight=["Indonesia", "Malaysia"],
)
```

`label` identifies observations in tooltips and supplies direct labels for
highlighted points. `series` groups observations by color.

## Formats and dimensions

Number formats accept `"auto"`, `"integer"`, `"decimal"`, `"percent"`,
`"currency"`, or a D3 number format string. Currency formatting requires an
ISO code:

```python
attaviz.bar(
    data,
    category="country",
    value="gdp",
    value_format="currency",
    currency="USD",
)
```

The default `width="responsive"` fills the parent HTML container. Pass a
numeric width for deterministic static exports. `frame()` resolves a responsive
chart to the theme's 600 px publication width because Vega-Lite does not
reliably support container sizing inside vertical compositions.

## Annotations and references

```python
chart = attaviz.add_annotation(
    chart,
    x=2020,
    y=275,
    text="Population passed 275 million",
    position="above",
)

chart = attaviz.add_reference_line(
    chart,
    value=300,
    axis="y",
    label="Projection",
)

chart = attaviz.add_reference_range(
    chart,
    start=250,
    end=300,
    axis="y",
    label="Expected range",
)
```

Annotations use data coordinates. Reference helpers require an explicit x or y
axis and compose with all three factory outputs.

## Publication frame

Apply `frame()` last to add accessibility metadata and publication details:

```python
chart = attaviz.frame(
    chart,
    description="A line chart showing population growth from 2010 to 2025.",
    source="World Bank",
    source_url="https://data.worldbank.org/",
    note="2025 values are estimates.",
    byline="Data team",
)
```

`description` is required and is exposed as Vega-Lite accessibility metadata.
The other fields are optional and appear beneath the chart, aligned with its
title. `source_url` is retained in Vega-Lite `usermeta` for host integrations;
native Vega-Lite titles do not support hyperlinks.
